newsitem.title: USA: Algae forces Fla. Power to shut down plants.
newsitem.headline: Algae forces Fla. Power to shut down plants.

text.p: A large algae bloom in the Gulf of Mexico has forced the shutdown of two Florida Power Corp plants in western Florida and caused the company to start power-saving measures affecting some 500,000 customers, the St. Petersburg Times reported Sunday.
Company officials could not be reached for comment Sunday.
Florida Power Corp is a unit of Florida Progress Corp.

Quoting a company spokesman, the newspaper said the two plants near the Anclote River had been shut down since Monday, when the algae moved into a canal that feeds cooling water into the two plants near Tarpon Springs.

To make up the 1,000 megawatts of generating power the plants normally provide, the company was turning to its load management program, in which customers receive rebates for allowing the utility to cut off power to certain appliances when needed.
The company said no one could predict how long the plants would have to remain down.
"We're just waiting for Mother Nature to do her thing," the company spokesman told the newspaper. "You can't go hook a rope to it (the algae bloom) and drag it back out to the Gulf."
He said environmental experts had said the bloom would die naturally, but that they were not sure when.
